about.title: Merced Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product does not care whether it fails in a Merced kitchen, on a job site off W 16th Street, or inside a car heading down G Street on a Friday afternoon. When a component breaks, a battery overheats, or a warning label leaves out the one thing you needed to know, the harm lands on the person holding it. Product liability claims in California generally rest on strict liability, which means you usually do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. Showing that the product carried a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury is typically what matters. Responsibility can also reach beyond the company whose name is on the box; distributors and the retailer who sold it may share liability. One practical step matters more than almost anything else: keep the product, its packaging, and any receipts exactly as they are. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys we connect Merced residents with work on contingency.

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: Under California law, a product claim usually turns on whether the item was defective and caused your injury, not on whether the company was negligent. The attorneys in our network know how to frame that question.

items.title: More Than One Party May Answer
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Merced retailer that sold the product can each be held responsible. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Evidence Is the Product Itself
items.desc: The failed item, its parts, and its packaging are the core of the case, so preserving them early matters. Getting connected quickly means that guidance comes before anything is thrown away.

items.question: My airbag did not deploy in a crash on R Street. Is that a product liability claim or a car accident claim?
items.answer: It can be both. Merced recorded 246 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involved vehicle components that did not perform as designed. If a defect in the airbag, seatbelt, or another part made your injuries worse, a strict liability claim against the maker may sit alongside any claim against another driver. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has reviewed it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew the product was dangerous?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often applies strict liability, so the injured person typically needs to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused the injury. Whether the company knew or was careless is usually not the central issue.
